transcript.text: Today we're going to learn how computers speak.
Binary language uses only two digits: zero and one.
Remember: everything a computer stores is always pure binary, no exceptions.
Every letter, pixel, and sound becomes a pattern of bits.
But in practice, not everything is stored as pure binary; real files wrap binary data in headers and metadata.
To write five in binary, we use one-zero-one.
Binary turns the physical world into digital information.
